mainEntity.name: What's the difference between BMR and calorie needs?

acceptedAnswer.text: BMR is the energy used at complete rest. Your actual daily calorie needs (TDEE) are higher because they include movement, exercise, and digestion.

mainEntity.name: Which BMR formula is most accurate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mifflin-St Jeor is widely used and performs well in validation studies, but no predictive BMR equation is universally most accurate for every person.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mifflin-St Jeor formula the most accurate?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a widely used general-population equation, but any formula is an estimate and individual energy needs can differ meaningfully from the prediction.

Increasing or preserving lean mass can affect resting energy expenditure, but the size of the change varies between people; strength training is useful for maintaining muscle and overall fitness, not a guarantee of a specific BMR increase.

mainEntity.name: How much does BMR typically decline with age?

acceptedAnswer.text: BMR tends to decline gradually with age, partly due to natural muscle loss over time — maintaining muscle mass through strength training can help offset this decline.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate my BMR by hand?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Mifflin-St Jeor: 10 x weight (kg) + 6.25 x height (cm) - 5 x age, then add 5 for men or subtract 161 for women. An 80 kg, 180 cm, 35-year-old man gets 1,755 kcal a day.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between BMR and RMR?

acceptedAnswer.text: BMR is measured under strict resting conditions, RMR under less strict ones. Prediction formulas are really estimating resting energy use, so the terms are often used interchangeably.

mainEntity.name: Why does Harris-Benedict give a different answer?

acceptedAnswer.text: It uses different coefficients from a different population. For a 28-year-old woman, 65 kg and 165 cm, Mifflin-St Jeor gives 1,380 kcal and revised Harris-Benedict about 1,439 kcal.
It depends on sex, age, height and weight. For a 30-year-old man of 178 cm, Mifflin-St Jeor gives about 1,518 to 1,918 kcal for weights from 55 to 95 kg.

mainEntity.name: How much does muscle raise BMR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only modestly. Using roughly 13 kcal per kg a day for muscle, 5 kg of extra muscle adds about 65 kcal a day.
